fact: The Ministry of Digital Affairs, through the universal service agency ABSU-CEP, put 43 community digital points and 43 free WiFi hotspots into service nationwide to give internet access to beneficiary communes and surrounding populations; the document does not call them rural.

The Benin government launched the World Bank-financed PITN2R on 18 December 2020, a US$47.20m five-year project to extend broadband connectivity in rural communities across 2,128 villages in five departments.
